title: The Human as the Purpose of Human Dignity
description: This paper offers a legal-philosophical and anthropological critique of the normative rupture introduced by the European AI Act. It argues that the regulation breaks with foundational legal concepts - especially the relationship between action, responsibility, and human dignity. Instead of applying a coherent understanding of law, the regulation projects human-rights qualities onto machines while reducing humans to administrable data subjects. The text contends that this is not merely a political misstep but an epistemological failure that erodes core legal categories such as agency, liability, and legitimacy. Drawing on classical legal and ethical concepts (e.g., auctoritas, dignitas, fas), the paper proposes a rethinking of law as a structural - not merely functional - medium that serves the human being as its end, not its instrument.
